item.dc:creator: Chloe Adams
item.description: In ancient times, trucks were tools for farmers and construction workers. The idea that they should offer amenities like air conditioning or power steering would have been questionable, and the suggestion of heated seats or ambient lighting would have been laughed off the assembly line.
item.content:encoded:
Briefing: In ancient times, trucks were tools for farmers and construction workers. The idea that they should offer amenities like air conditioning or power steering would have been questionable, and the suggestion of heated seats or ambient lighting would have been laughed off the assembly line.

In ancient times, trucks were tools for farmers and construction workers. The idea that they should offer amenities like air conditioning or power steering would have been questionable, and the suggestion of heated seats or ambient lighting would have been laughed off the assembly line. We live in a gentler era, though, and the 2027 Chevy Silverado 1500 reflects the mainstream popularity of pickups for both work and play. Chevy’s half-ton lineup gets a major overhaul for the coming model year with reshaped sheetmetal; redesigned interiors featuring carbon fiber, wood, and bright pops of color; and two brand-new small-block V-8s that will delight internal-combustion loyalists.

Chevy has made enough changes to the Silverado for 2027 to call it a new generation, although what generation that is depends on if you’re starting your count from the first introduction of Silverado as its own model (1998) or all the way back to the first use of the name (1975, as a trim on the C/K models). We’re going from the ’90s, which would make this new truck the fifth generation. To earn its generational title, the Silverado wears a new exterior, crisp as a starched shirt, set off by LED lights, burly wheel lip moldings, and a redesigned bumper. Underneath, the chassis will be familiar from the previous year, albeit with some suspension tweaks for more stable towing and a better ride.

HWA has made a name for itself by developing, building, and racing Mercedes-AMGs, and by producing the iconic, road-legal CLK GTR Straßenversion. It then ventured into the restomodding world with its limited-run, reborn 190E Evo II and is now turning its attention to a new project. This one appears to be a modern interpretation of the legendary AMG Hammer and it should get AMG fans very excited. The original Hammer launched in the mid-1980s as the ultimate version of the W124 sedan.

AMG was still an independent firm at the time, before Mercedes-Benz absorbed it. The car, officially badged the 300E 5.6 AMG, ditched the original naturally aspirated 3.0-liter inline-6 in favor of a 5.5-liter V8. This engine made 355 horsepower and 388 pound-feet of torque, enough for the rear-wheel-drive beast to hit 60 mph in just five seconds. It quickly earned a nickname of 'The Hammer' and was later updated with a 6.0-liter engine making 385 hp and 420 lb-ft. It's a true AMG icon and is perhaps the perfect next project for HWA.

For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field. Some of these lookalikes, cars like the orange and white 1969 Chevy Camaro SS/RS, and the the black and silver 1978 Corvette pace car replica , are blue-chip collector classics. Others, like this Oldsmobile Calais 500 , which is up for auction through Bring a Trailer, are rarely remembered.

Oldsmobile reportedly built 2,998 Calais 500 commemorative pace car editions (confusingly, some sources say just 242), though none of them looked anything like the real version. The genuine Indy Calais driven by Rockford Files star James Garner, (there were actually two cars) was a special convertible version that Olds never offered to the public.

Appealing to enthusiasts and buyers of performance cars is already hard enough with internal combustion engines, whether we're talking affordable hot hatchbacks or high-end supercars. As many automakers have been learning the hard way, it's orders of magnitude tougher to build and sell a good electric car to those same enthusiasts. They want their cars to feel real , with tactile sensations and character and emotion and all those other valid clichés, and few (if any) EVs have achieved that or even really gotten close.

Now, the wizards at Affalterbach have done it. The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe has unbelievable performance figures when it comes to power and speed as well as efficiency and charging, it has advanced technology features and F1-derived aerodynamics, and months after the reveal its design still has everybody talking, to say the least. Most importantly, it is absolute dynamite to drive – a grand slam, a home run, the automotive equivalent of an EGOT, however else you want to say it – and much of that is down to how it emulates a combustion powertrain, complete with V8 noises and shifts that will stretch your definition of "real."

On Wednesday, NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory , a space telescope that's been in orbit since 2004, finally re-entered Earth's atmosphere above Indonesia. However, it appears to have done so with a risk of casualties five times beyond what NASA technical standards mandate. How and why this happened isn't immediately clear; NASA Public Affairs Specialist Alise Fisher told Jalopnik, "In the leadup to Swift's Nov. 20, 2004, launch, NASA determined the risk was consistent with mission requirements as allowed by agency policy." Somewhere between launch and reentry, that risk assessment shifted. It's unlikely that anybody made a specific mistake; this is probably the result of, well, space being hard. Still, it does highlight that our main defense against the detritus of astronomical ambitions is pure luck.

Swift is only crashing to Earth because it ran out of fuel to stay in orbit or adjust its trajectory. To NASA's credit, it did throw $30 million at a private company in an unprecedented attempt to rescue Swift with another satellite that would pull it back up into safe orbit. Sadly, the rescue satellite itself failed, dooming Swift to this fate.

Spain’s Nabrawind has developed a way to install exceptionally tall wind turbine towers without bringing an enormous crawler crane to the site. Its Nabralift system uses a tubular upper tower supported by a three-legged steel structure. Hydraulic equipment raises the assembled turbine while modular sections are inserted below it near ground level. The lifting frame can then be removed and used on another installation. This addresses genuine logistical and construction problems, particularly at remote sites where specialist cranes are expensive to transport and where wind can interrupt conventional lifting operations.

The company has progressed beyond demonstration-scale hardware. In September 2026, UL Solutions issued type certification for Envision’s 7.8 MW turbine on Nabrawind’s 188-meter tower. Fortescue is using 17 of those tower configurations at the 133 MW Nullagine wind project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region, where construction is underway. Two-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriqs are not included in the recall, and the only Blazer EV trims involved are SS and Police Pursuit Vehicles.

The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.
